title: The PCP Exam, Part 2: Heart, Abdomen, Limbs and Nerves

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already check pulse, motor and sensation in each limb, and feel the abdomen for tenderness. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Examine the heart and circulation: JVD, heart sounds, pulses, edema
  2. Examine the abdomen and limbs in the right order and spot danger signs
  3. Do a focused neuro exam that feeds the stroke protocol

Textbook: Chapter 16, from the Cardiovascular exam to Limits of the Physical Examination (ends PDF p. 1494)
slides.say: Welcome back. Last lesson we examined the head, neck and chest. Today we finish the exam. As EMRs, you already check pulse, movement and feeling in every limb, and you already feel the abdomen for tenderness. As a PCP, you'll go further. We'll cover three things: how to examine the heart and circulation, including neck veins, heart sounds and swelling; how to examine the abdomen and limbs in the right order and spot the danger signs; and a focused neurological exam that feeds straight into the BC stroke protocol and into your reassessment after every treatment.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。上节课我们查了头、颈和胸部，今天把体检做完。作为 EMR，你们已经会查每个肢体的脉搏、运动和感觉，也会摸腹部找压痛。作为 PCP，要再往前走。今天讲三件事：怎样检查心脏和循环，包括颈静脉、心音和水肿；怎样按正确顺序检查腹部和四肢、认出危险征象；以及一套有重点的神经系统检查，它直接连到 BC 的卒中流程，也连到你每次处置之后的复评。

slides.title: Neck veins, pulses and age
slides.body:
• JVD + low BP → think cardiogenic shock
  • JVD + low BP after chest trauma → tension pneumothorax or tamponade
  • Hypotension can hide JVD: flat veins rule nothing out
  • Compare pulses left vs right, and near vs far
  • Older adults compensate poorly; children compensate too well
slides.say: Let's start with circulation. Jugular venous distention, or JVD, means blood is backing up before the right side of the heart. With low blood pressure, think of cardiogenic shock, where the pump is failing. After chest trauma, the same pair suggests a tension pneumothorax or cardiac tamponade, which is blood squeezing the heart. But a hypotensive patient may have flat neck veins, so no JVD rules nothing out. Compare pulses left with right, and near with far. And remember age: older adults can't tighten their vessels well, so they crash sooner, while children compensate so well that they look less sick than they are.
slides.sayZh: 先从循环开始。颈静脉怒张（JVD）说明血在右心之前淤积。如果同时血压低，要想到心源性休克，也就是泵衰竭。胸部外伤后出现同样的组合，提示张力性气胸或心脏压塞（血液压迫心脏）。但低血压的病人颈静脉可能是瘪的，所以没有 JVD 不能排除任何问题。脉搏要左右比、近端远端比。还要记住年龄：老人血管收缩能力差，垮得更快；孩子代偿能力太强，看起来没有实际那么重。

slides.title: Heart sounds: what's extra?
slides.body:
S1 S2lub-DUBnormal
S3just after S2heart failure; abnormal over 35
S4just before S1always abnormal: stiff ventricle
  • Aortic: 2nd space, right of sternum; pulmonic: 2nd space, left
  • Tricuspid: lower left sternal border; mitral: apex
  • Murmur = turbulence at a valve; bruit = in a narrowed artery
slides.say: Next, heart sounds. The normal pair is S1 and S2, the lub-dub. Extra sounds matter. S3 comes just after S2; it can be normal in healthy young people, but over age thirty-five it points to heart failure. S4 comes just before S1, and it's always abnormal: the left ventricle has become stiff. Listen at four valve areas: aortic at the second space right of the sternum, pulmonic at the second space left, tricuspid at the lower left sternal border, and mitral at the apex. A murmur is turbulence at a valve; a bruit is turbulence in a narrowed artery, like the carotid.
slides.sayZh: 接下来是心音。正常的一对是 S1 和 S2，也就是「扑通」。多出来的声音才要紧。S3 紧跟在 S2 之后，健康年轻人可以有，但三十五岁以上出现就提示心衰。S4 紧挨在 S1 之前，任何时候都不正常，说明左心室变僵硬了。在四个瓣膜区听：主动脉瓣在胸骨右缘第二肋间，肺动脉瓣在胸骨左缘第二肋间，三尖瓣在胸骨左下缘，二尖瓣在心尖。杂音（murmur）是瓣膜处的湍流；血管杂音（bruit）是狭窄动脉里的湍流，比如颈动脉。

slides.title: The abdomen: change the order
slides.body:
Inspect→Auscultate→Percuss→Palpate
  • Ask where it hurts most; touch that spot last
  • Start in the quadrant farthest from the pain; watch the face
  • Guarding, rigidity, rebound → irritated peritoneum
  • Colic: restless; peritonitis: lies very still
  • Bowel sounds: little value, but BC excuses only EMRs from listening
slides.say: The abdomen is the one place where the order changes: inspect, listen, percuss, and only then palpate, because pressing first can change what you hear. Ask the patient to point to where it hurts most, and touch that spot last. Start in the quadrant farthest from the pain, and watch the face, not your hands. Guarding, rigidity, which means a board-like belly, and rebound pain when you let go all suggest an irritated peritoneum, the lining of the belly. Behaviour helps too: a patient with colic, like a kidney stone, keeps moving, while a patient with peritonitis lies very still. Bowel sounds tell you little on scene, but the BC grading criteria excuse only EMR candidates from listening to the abdomen, so as a PCP, include it.
slides.sayZh: 腹部是唯一要换顺序的地方：视诊、听诊、叩诊，最后才触诊，因为先按压会改变你听到的声音。让病人指出最痛的地方，那个点最后才碰。从离痛点最远的象限开始，眼睛看病人的脸，而不是看你的手。肌紧张、强直（肚子硬得像木板），以及松手时的反跳痛，都提示腹膜（腹腔的内衬）受到刺激。病人的表现也有帮助：绞痛的病人，比如肾结石，会不停地动；腹膜炎的病人则一动不动地躺着。肠鸣音在现场提供的信息不多，但 BC 评分标准只免除了 EMR 考生的腹部听诊，所以作为 PCP，这一步要做。

slides.title: Abdomen: don't miss these
slides.body:
• Pulsing mass in the upper midline → aneurysm: palpate gently, minimally
  • The aorta lies behind the peritoneum: a normal front exam can't clear it
  • Liver or spleen bleeding may show few signs until the belly swells
  • Lower pain in a woman of childbearing age → think ectopic pregnancy
  • Genitals: inspect only, with a partner present, only when needed
slides.say: Some abdominal findings you can't afford to miss. A pulsing mass in the upper middle of the abdomen suggests an aortic aneurysm, so palpate gently and as little as possible. The aorta sits behind the peritoneum, so a normal exam of the front of the belly can't rule it out. A bleeding liver or spleen may cause few signs at first, until the belly starts to swell. In a woman of childbearing age with lower abdominal pain, think of an ectopic pregnancy. And examine the genitals only when really needed, like heavy bleeding or an imminent birth: inspection only, with a partner present.
slides.sayZh: 有些腹部发现绝不能漏。上腹正中摸到搏动性肿块，提示主动脉瘤，所以触诊要轻、越少越好。主动脉位于腹膜后方，所以腹部前面检查正常也不能排除它。肝或脾出血起初可能没什么体征，直到肚子开始胀起来。育龄女性下腹痛，要想到异位妊娠。生殖器只在真正需要时才查，比如大出血或即将分娩：只做视诊，并有搭档在场。

slides.q: A 68-year-old man has sudden, severe back and belly pain. He is pale and sweaty, and you see a pulsing mass in his upper abdomen. What is the best approach?
options: Palpate deeply to estimate the mass's size
Touch it gently and minimally, and treat this as time-critical
Listen for bowel sounds for two full minutes first
Have him walk to the stretcher to save time
slides.say: Let's pause for a question. A sixty-eight-year-old man has sudden, severe back and belly pain. He is pale and sweaty, and you see a pulsing mass in his upper abdomen. What is the best approach? A, palpate deeply to estimate the mass's size. B, touch it gently and minimally, and treat this as time-critical. C, listen for bowel sounds for two full minutes first. D, have him walk to the stretcher to save time. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停一下考考你：一位六十八岁男性突然剧烈腰背痛和腹痛，面色苍白、出汗，你看到他上腹有搏动性肿块。最好的做法是什么？A 深压触诊估计肿块大小；B 轻触、尽量少碰，把它当作分秒必争的病人；C 先听两分钟肠鸣音；D 让他走到担架上以节省时间。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Sudden pain, signs of shock and a pulsing upper abdominal mass suggest a leaking aortic aneurysm, so you handle it gently, as little as possible, and move quickly. A, deep palpation, could make the leak worse. C wastes time on a finding with little value on scene. D adds strain to a patient who may be in shock.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。突发疼痛、休克征象加上上腹搏动性肿块，提示主动脉瘤在渗漏，所以要轻柔、尽量少碰，并且快速行动。A 深压可能让渗漏更严重；C 把时间浪费在一个院前价值不大的发现上；D 给可能已经休克的病人增加负担。

slides.title: Limbs: bones and joints
slides.body:
• Point tenderness = most reliable sign of a closed fracture
  • Open fracture: bone through skin, or any wound near a suspected fracture
  • Pathologic fracture: normal force, weak bone (osteoporosis, cancer)
  • Pulse, motor, sensation before and after every splint
  • Dislocated shoulder: looks squared off
  • Pain on any movement → stop and immobilize
slides.say: Now the limbs. The most reliable sign of a closed fracture is point tenderness, pain at one exact spot when you press. A fracture counts as open if bone breaks the skin, or if there's any wound near a suspected fracture. Watch for pathologic fractures, where normal force breaks weak bone, for example in osteoporosis or cancer. As an EMR, you already check pulse, motor and sensation. As a PCP, document them before and after every splint, and compare with the other side. A dislocated shoulder often looks squared off. And if any movement causes pain, stop and immobilize.
slides.sayZh: 接下来是四肢。闭合性骨折最可靠的体征是点状压痛，也就是按压时某一个精确的点疼。骨头穿出皮肤，或者疑似骨折附近有任何伤口，都算开放性骨折。要留意病理性骨折：正常的力量折断了有病的骨头，比如骨质疏松或癌症。作为 EMR，你已经会查脉搏、运动和感觉；作为 PCP，每次上夹板前后都要记录，并和对侧比较。肩关节脱位常看起来是「方肩」。任何动作引起疼痛，就停下来固定。

slides.title: Circulation in the limbs
slides.body:
Cold, pale, painful limb: the 5 Ps

  • Pain, pallor, paresthesia or paralysis, poikilothermia (cold)
  • Pulselessness comes last: don't wait for it
  • Pitting edema: press 5 s or more; +1 (up to 7.5 mm) to +4 (over 30 mm)
  • Both legs swollen → whole-body cause: heart failure, cirrhosis
  • One leg swollen → local cause: a blocked deep vein
slides.say: A sudden blockage of an artery gives the five Ps: pain, pallor, paresthesia or paralysis, which means tingling or weakness, poikilothermia, which means the limb goes as cold as the room, and pulselessness. The pulse is the last thing to go, so act before it disappears. For edema, press your thumb into the foot or shin for five seconds or more. Plus one is a pit up to seven and a half millimetres; plus four is more than thirty. Swelling in both legs suggests a whole-body cause, like heart failure; swelling in one leg suggests a local cause, like a blocked deep vein.
slides.sayZh: 动脉突然堵塞会出现 5P：疼痛、苍白、感觉异常或瘫痪（也就是麻刺或无力）、变温（肢体凉得和环境一样），以及无脉。脉搏是最后才消失的，所以要在它消失之前就行动。查水肿时，用拇指按压足背或胫前五秒以上：加一是凹陷不超过七点五毫米，加四是超过三十毫米。双腿都肿提示全身性原因，比如心衰；只有一条腿肿提示局部原因，比如深静脉堵塞。

slides.title: The focused neuro exam
slides.body:
1. Level of consciousness: AVPU or GCS; posture
  2. Cranial nerves: pupils, eye movements, smile, speech, swallow, shrug
  3. Motor: strength in each limb, side to side; pronator drift
  4. Coordination: finger-to-nose
  5. Sensation: left vs right, near vs far

Keep asking: is it symmetrical?
slides.say: The neuro exam can feel huge, but a focused version takes only a few minutes. Start with level of consciousness, using AVPU or the Glasgow Coma Scale, and look at posture. Then a quick cranial nerve check: pupils, eye movements, a smile, speech, swallowing, and a shoulder shrug. Test strength in each limb against resistance, and check pronator drift: the patient closes the eyes and holds both arms straight out. A weak arm drifts down. Check coordination with finger-to-nose, and compare sensation left with right. Through all of it, keep asking: is it symmetrical?
slides.sayZh: 神经系统检查听起来很庞大，但有重点的版本几分钟就能做完。先看意识水平，用 AVPU 或格拉斯哥昏迷评分，并观察姿势。然后快速查脑神经：瞳孔、眼球运动、微笑、说话、吞咽、耸肩。逐个肢体对抗阻力测肌力，再查旋前漂移：让病人闭眼、双臂向前伸直，无力的那只手臂会往下沉。用指鼻试验查协调，左右对比感觉。整个过程中一直问自己：两边对称吗？

slides.title: Reading the neuro findings
slides.body:
• One-sided face/arm weakness + speech trouble → stroke
  • Altered mental status often isn't neurological: perfusion, sepsis, sugar
  • Delirium = sudden, with a cause; dementia = slow decline
  • Trauma, global drop in LOC → something growing in the skull
  • Limb weakness with sensory loss → spinal cord
  • Babinski sign in an adult = brain or cord damage
slides.say: Weakness of the face and arm on one side, with trouble speaking, is the classic picture of stroke. But altered mental status is often not a brain problem at all: poor perfusion, early sepsis in older adults, or low blood sugar can all cause it. Separate delirium, a sudden change with a clear cause, from dementia, a slow decline. In trauma, a drop in overall consciousness suggests something growing inside the skull, such as a bleed. Limb weakness with loss of feeling suggests the spinal cord. And in an adult, a positive Babinski sign, the big toe going up, means brain or cord damage.
slides.sayZh: 一侧面部和手臂无力、加上说话困难，是卒中的典型表现。但意识改变常常根本不是脑的问题：灌注不足、老人的早期脓毒症或低血糖都能引起。要分清谵妄（突然改变、有明确诱因）和痴呆（缓慢衰退）。创伤病人整体意识下降，提示颅内有东西在变大，比如出血。肢体无力伴感觉丧失提示脊髓问题。成人巴宾斯基征阳性（大脚趾往上翘）说明脑或脊髓受损。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: the Stroke protocol
slides.body:
BC Stroke protocol: any neuro deficit, altered LOC, airway or breathing trouble, or a weak, rapid or absent radial pulse.

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Assess and manage ABCs
  • Oxygen to SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  • Position the patient
  • Blood glucose check
  • Recognize it with FAST-VAN
  • Timely transport; notify the hospital en route

PCP adds (en route)

  • Vascular access
  • Site above the wrist
  • 18 G catheter
  • Preferably on the right side
slides.say: Here's how your neuro exam connects to BC protocol. The Stroke protocol applies to any neurological deficit, an altered level of consciousness, airway or breathing trouble, or a weak, rapid or absent radial pulse. Every licence level manages the ABCs, gives oxygen to keep the saturation at ninety-four or above, positions the patient, checks the blood glucose, uses FAST-VAN to recognize the stroke, and transports quickly, notifying the hospital on the way. The PCP adds vascular access, and BC is specific: en route, above the wrist, with an eighteen gauge catheter, preferably on the right side.
slides.sayZh: 这是神经系统检查和 BC 流程的衔接。卒中流程适用于任何神经功能缺损、意识水平改变、气道或呼吸困难，或桡动脉搏动弱、快或摸不到。所有级别都要：处理 ABC、给氧使血氧维持在九十四以上、摆体位、测血糖、用 FAST-VAN 识别卒中、及时转运并在途中通知医院。PCP 多做的是建立静脉通路，而且 BC 规定得很具体：在转运途中、选手腕以上的部位、用十八号针、最好在右侧。

slides.q: You're a PCP. A 74-year-old woman has sudden left arm drift and slurred speech that began 40 minutes ago. BGL 6.2 mmol/L, SpO₂ 97%. What is the best plan?
options: Start an 18 G IV in her right hand on scene, then move her
Go now; en route, an 18 G IV above the wrist, preferably right
No vascular access: it isn't in the stroke protocol
Give D10W first, in case it's low sugar
slides.say: Let's try a PCP decision. A seventy-four-year-old woman has sudden left arm drift and slurred speech that began forty minutes ago. Her glucose is six point two, and her saturation is ninety-seven percent. What is the best plan? A, start an eighteen gauge IV in her right hand on scene, then move her. B, go now, and en route, start an eighteen gauge IV above the wrist, preferably on the right. C, no vascular access, since it isn't in the stroke protocol. D, give D10W first, in case it's low sugar. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。一位七十四岁女性四十分钟前突然出现左臂漂移和口齿不清。血糖六点二，血氧百分之九十七。最好的方案是什么？A 在现场先在她右手背打一个十八号静脉针，再搬运；B 立即出发，途中在手腕以上、最好右侧打十八号静脉针；C 不建静脉通路，因为卒中流程里没有；D 先给 D10W，以防是低血糖。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. BC puts the PCP's vascular access for stroke en route: above the wrist, eighteen gauge, preferably on the right. A is wrong twice: it delays transport, and the hand is below the wrist. C is wrong because vascular access is exactly what the PCP adds in this protocol. D is wrong because her glucose of six point two is normal; D10W is for confirmed hypoglycemia, under four point zero.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。BC 规定 PCP 给卒中病人建静脉通路是在转运途中：手腕以上、十八号针、最好在右侧。A 错了两处：耽误转运，而且手背在手腕以下。C 错在静脉通路恰恰是 PCP 在这个流程里多做的事。D 错在她的血糖六点二是正常的；D10W 用于确认的低血糖，也就是低于四点零。

slides.title: Children, records and limits
slides.body:
• Ages 1–3: examine toe to head; keep the parent close
  • From about 4–5: head to toe usually works
  • Be honest: if it will hurt, say so
  • Record objective findings and pertinent negatives
  • The exam has limits: pair it with the history
  • BC PCPs add a functional enquiry by body system
slides.say: Toddlers, from one to three, fear strangers most, so examine them from toe to head and keep the parent close. From about four or five, you can usually go head to toe. Be honest: if something will hurt, say so. When you record, write the objective findings and the pertinent negatives, the important things you checked and didn't find, like no JVD or clear lungs. And know the limits: the exam can't find everything. It works best with the history, which for a BC PCP includes a functional enquiry by body system. More on that in Chapter seventeen.
slides.sayZh: 一到三岁的幼儿最怕陌生人，所以从脚往头查，并让家长待在旁边。大约四五岁起，通常可以从头到脚查。要诚实：会疼就直说。记录时写客观发现和有意义的阴性发现，也就是你查了、确认没有的重要项目，比如没有 JVD、双肺清。还要知道局限：体检不能发现一切，要和病史结合才最有效；对 BC 的 PCP 来说，病史还包括按身体系统进行的系统问诊。第十七章再详细讲。

slides.title: Reassess after every treatment
slides.body:
After you give…Recheck
Salbutamol, CPAPRate, effort, lung sounds, speech, SpO₂, vitals
Fluid bolusReassess every 500 mL; listen to the lungs
Oral glucose, D10W, glucagonBlood glucose and level of consciousness
NitroglycerinPain and BP before each dose

The patient says it isn't better? Believe them and reassess.
slides.say: An exam isn't done once. As a PCP, every treatment is a test, and you have to read the result. After salbutamol or CPAP, recheck the breathing rate, effort, lung sounds, ability to speak, saturation and vital signs; the BC CPAP guideline builds reassessment into every step. During a fluid bolus, BC asks you to reassess every five hundred millilitres, and listen to the lungs, too. After any glucose treatment, recheck the sugar and the level of consciousness. Before each nitroglycerin dose, check the pain and the blood pressure. And if your patient says they're no better, believe them.
slides.sayZh: 体检不是做一次就完。作为 PCP，每一次处置都是一次测试，你得读出结果。给了沙丁胺醇或 CPAP 之后，复查呼吸频率、费力程度、呼吸音、说话能力、血氧和生命体征；BC 的 CPAP 指引把复评写进了每一步。补液时，BC 要求每五百毫升复评一次，也要听肺。任何补糖处置之后，复查血糖和意识水平。每次给硝酸甘油之前，先查疼痛和血压。病人说没好转时，要相信他。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Low BP can hide JVD: flat neck veins don't rule things out
  • Older adults on BP pills compensate poorly and crash sooner
  • A soft, normal front abdomen doesn't clear the aorta
  • Stroke-like signs? Check glucose first
  • Stroke IV goes in en route, never at the cost of scene time
  • Cold, pale, painful limb: don't wait for pulselessness
slides.say: Here are the new watch-outs. First, low blood pressure can hide JVD, so flat neck veins don't rule anything out. Second, older adults, especially on blood pressure medicines, compensate poorly and can crash with little warning, while children hide shock until late. Third, a soft, normal-looking abdomen doesn't clear the aorta. Fourth, before you call something a stroke, check the glucose; low sugar can look exactly like a stroke, and the check is in the BC protocol for every licence level. Fifth, the stroke IV goes in en route. And in a cold, pale, painful limb, act early; pulselessness comes last.
slides.sayZh: 新的注意事项如下。第一，低血压可以掩盖 JVD，所以颈静脉瘪也不能排除任何问题。第二，老人，尤其是吃降压药的，代偿能力差，可能几乎没有预兆就垮掉；而孩子会把休克藏到很晚。第三，腹部摸着软、看着正常，并不能排除主动脉问题。第四，判断卒中之前先测血糖；低血糖可以和卒中一模一样，而且测血糖是 BC 流程里所有级别都要做的。第五，卒中病人的静脉针在途中打。还有，肢体又凉、又白、又痛时要早行动，无脉是最后才出现的。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Circulation: read JVD in context; S3 over 35 or any S4 is abnormal
  2. Abdomen: inspect, listen, percuss, then palpate; the aorta hides behind
  3. Neuro exam feeds the stroke protocol: glucose for all; PCP IV en route

Next: Chapter 17, Patient Assessment
slides.say: Let's wrap up with three things to remember. One: for circulation, read JVD in context, know that an S3 over age thirty-five or any S4 is abnormal. Two: in the abdomen, inspect, listen and percuss before you palpate, start far from the pain, and remember the aorta hides behind the belly. Three: your neuro exam feeds the BC stroke protocol. Everyone checks the glucose; the PCP adds an eighteen gauge IV above the wrist, preferably right, en route. Next, Chapter seventeen: patient assessment. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，循环方面：结合情况解读 JVD；三十五岁以上出现 S3、或任何 S4 都是异常。二，腹部：先视、听、叩，最后才触诊，从离痛点最远处开始，记住主动脉藏在后面。三，神经系统检查直接连到 BC 卒中流程：所有级别都测血糖，PCP 在途中于手腕以上、最好右侧打十八号静脉针。下一课是第十七章：患者评估。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
